utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me give three decisions. Let us move to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please sit. And you may begin, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, I'll have to call you MLD1. As you know, my name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys for the accused Milan Lukic. Again, I have to call you MLD1 to protect your identity from disclosure. Towards that end, if I could have the court usher's assistance, I'd like to hand you a pseudonym sheet and ask you to take a look at that, sir. When you receive that from the court usher, I would ask you to review the same and verify that the information as to your identity contained therein is true and accurate, and then let me know. Then if I can have you, sir, please sign that document so that I can ask for it to be admitted under seal so that that information will not be available to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would then move for this document once signed to be submitted under the next available 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D100, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if we could begin with the part of your testimony. If you could please state for the record, what is your ethnic and religious affiliation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Bosnian Muslim. I'm a Bosniak of the Muslim faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And also for the record, without revealing the actual address where you live or any other information that might reveal your identity, could you tell us generally which city and state you currently reside in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Bosnia, in the environs of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise for the pause. We have to wait for the translation and the transcript, so if I pause at any time it's for that, and you need not pay any heed. Now, for the record could you also tell us if in fact you lived in this location, that is the environs of Sarajevo, in 1992 or if you lived elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No, I lived in Visegrad [Realtime transcript read in error, "Vlad"].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I believe that line 20 should be "Visegrad" rather than "Vlad," for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, again, without telling us anything about yourself that could reveal your identity - you are testifying here as a protected witness at your request - could you please tell us the reasons behind your seeking protective measures to testify for the Defence of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Because of my safety, because nothing nice is being said about Milan Lukic about the -- among the Muslims, so if they found out what I'm doing now, it would not be good for me. I have come to say what I know, and looking around and watching television and knowing what he is being charged with, I would like to say what I know about this time that I spent some time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise, Your Honours. It looks like some portion of what he has said has not come into the transcript. He mentioned dates. Perhaps we'll -- that's perhaps easier corrected by me asking a follow-up question instead of trying to recollect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned some dates and a time-period that you spent with Milan in response to my last question. Can you repeat that as it has not -- that portion of your response has not made it into the official transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: From the 4th to the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, now, with respect to -- you indicated nothing nice is being said about Lukic among the Muslims. Do you have any specific examples or specific experiences wherein you have personal or firsthand knowledge of what kinds of things are being said about Milan Lukic or his Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection as to relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I recall, the Trial Chamber back - I can't remember what date it was - advised that we should definitely bring to the Court's attention any factors we have of outside pressures on witnesses or outside pressures in the communities that the witnesses come from that would create difficulty for them to come to testify, and I believe that this witness has some knowledge of general threats made as to witnesses or anyone who would be willing to come forward to testify in these proceedings for the Defence of Milan Lukic, and with that I just ask if he does. Depending on his answer, obviously it may not -- it may or may not advance the matter any further, but I'm just complying with the directive that I bring any such matters to the Court's attention so they have an overall picture of the scenario under which the Defence is proceeding in the field, trying to find witnesses or trying to obtain the attendance of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see it as being very relevant, probably only marginally so. Let's hear the witness's answer. Do you remember the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you remember the question that was asked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why I'm seeking protective measures?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not it. I'll just ask counsel to repeat it very succinctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The question I had, sir, is as a follow-up to you telling us why you had requested protective measures, is there anything that you personally saw or experienced that solidified your desire to have protective measures as to the manner in which persons -- outside persons were talking about Milan Lukic and/or his Defence. I just caution you, when my microphone is on, please don't speak so your voice does not go out on the public transmission.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, in the area where I'm living now, I was -- I was in the company of people of my faith, Muslims, if you know what I'm saying, and for example, there was stories when they -- when they hear something nice about Milan Lukic, they don't like to hear it. They would be able to liquidate that person or maybe attack the children, something like that. I was in the company of such people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and they had said -- I mean, that's why I asked to have protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please move on to another topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could move into private session to protect the identity of the witness. I have some matters relating to his background and residence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, what is the evidence that you intend to lead in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The witness in general or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, his -- oh, his girlfriend.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct, the identity of the girlfriend might reveal his identity is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Do you have something more specific to lead in relation to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the events -- the events that the witness has knowledge of experience with the girlfriend. She's -- throughout the story -- when I interviewed the witness, throughout the story he kept repeating her name, so the point was if he repeats her name, if someone knows the relationship between them, they can identify the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. I was wondering the about the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The evidence that you have to lead in relation to her is relevant to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. She was also a witness to the -- she accompanied the witness in the events that he is to testify about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, just a few general questions about Visegrad and the time-period that you mentioned. Can you describe for us the general situation in Visegrad when the Uzice Corps came to that city, and if you recall the time-period, if you could state that as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, the situation was not good. There was shooting. You could hear shooting. It was possible to be arrested. The situation was unstable. It was war. You couldn't go where you wanted and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And upon the withdrawal of the Uzice Corps, who was in control of the municipality of Visegrad at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: After the withdrawal of the Uzice Corps, the civilian authorities were in power.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What ethnic group did the civilian authorities belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was there a particular political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: The SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the civilian authorities, do you recall who the chief of the police or any of the commanders in the police force were after the withdrawal of the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Tomic and -- I can't remember the names now. I know it's Tomic and others. I mean, he was the person considered to be in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to -- prior to 1992, did you know a man named Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him before that as I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you said you didn't know him before that date that you'd mentioned. Could you again tell us when it was that you first met or encountered Milan Lukic and the circumstances of that first encounter with Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I was in the apartment of my fiancee. Well, you know the person that I mean. On the 4th of June, three uniformed persons came. Two were not so tall, and one was tall, heavily built [as interpreted] with brown hair, and they were checking our IDs, not only our IDs, but of everyone in the building. When they checked the personal ID cards and so on, the two shorter guys said that they would need to take us somewhere, something like the police, something like that, and then when this taller guy heard that, he said that he also wanted to look at our documents, and that's what he did, and he said that the documents were all right. There was nothing disputable there. So then I asked those two shorter guys -- actually, he asked those two shorter guys to leave, to go outside, that he needed to speak to us. So they did as he asked them. They went out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could back up, just -- you utilised the word in Bosnian "krupan" to describe this individual. I don't see that it's necessarily gone into the transcript correctly as it has been translated. Well, what does "krupan" mean in the Bosnian dialect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I note, Your Honours, at page 11 line 9 it's in the transcript as "heavily built," so I'd ask that be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we get back to the encounter with these three uniformed individuals at the apartment of your girlfriend, first of all, how were these men attired that day? You said they were uniformed. What kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Blue police uniforms, militia uniforms [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, Your Honours, page 12, line 7, he said blue uniforms, police uniforms with militia on the side. I see in the transcript it says -- militia on the sleeve. It just says "militia uniforms" in the transcript. I'd ask for that to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what time of day, sir, these individuals arrived at the apartment of your girlfriend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Sometime in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if -- pardon me. Did you recognise any of the persons that arrived that asked to check for your identification that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No, I did not recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what did you and/or your girlfriend do when these policemen asked you to come down to the station with them? What was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, we were horrified. By looking at her, I think my girlfriend was scared even more than me. She started crying, and I felt bad about her and about myself. When this tall guy saw that, he asked the other two guys to leave so that he could have a word with us and so that he could check whether our documents were in order. Luckily, they followed his instructions. They left and waited outside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did that individual, the taller individual who remained, did he have any further communications with you, and in particular, did he identify himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's just what I was about to say. When the other two men left, he introduced himself saying his name was Milan Lukic and that he was just back from Switzerland. He said he had been mobilised into this - what shall I call it - coalition against his will, that his mother was sick and that's why he was now back in order to take her to Belgrade for treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did he tell you anything else as to -- as regarding you and your girlfriend, and did he give any instructions or advice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: He advised us not to go anywhere and told us to go to an abandoned house not far from there. Once he had introduced himself and once he had told us what he was there for, then I asked him whether he could save us in any way or help us escape from Visegrad, you see, because it wasn't safe. He said he would try but he would need some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did he at any point in time indicate why he was willing to assist you in such a manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No, not really. I later realised that he knew my girlfriend. He used to see her at work in this cafe where she worked. I realised at one point that it wouldn't be a problem when he started getting into details, and he helped me feel safer. To be perfectly honest, when someone saves you, you are glad. One couldn't just leave town. One could get into town but not leave. You needed these documents and those documents and a lot of different documents. Some people will let you have them and some people won't, and then I kept thinking to myself, He is a Serb after all, and you know, I couldn't help thinking to myself, Will this work or not, but what prevailed was my ambition to save my --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness probably means "girlfriend."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, this weighed much more heavily upon me among all the other suspicions that I had and everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you indicated that on the way to Uvac that Milan Lukic went into details about knowing your girlfriend and that you felt safer as a result. Did that occur on the same day that the three police officers came to your home, or was that -- strike that. Let me -- let me back up and try and short-circuit the questioning somewhat. You indicated earlier that he told you to go to an abandoned house that was nearby. Did you in fact go to that abandoned house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We spent three days there. We waited because he said he would give us a hand and take us away, and we were waiting for him to show up with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic return as you had earlier agreed, and if so, what date was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. He was back three days later with his mother. Nevertheless, he told us that he had been unable to provide the documents for us. He only had documents for himself and his mother. He did, however, bring some clothes for this girlfriend of mine, you know which one, the sort of clothes worn by Serb women, if you get my meaning. I don't think she could have been saved or taken anywhere else because she would have been quite conspicuous in those broad trousers normally worn by Muslim women.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you explain for us briefly for those of us not familiar with "dimije" what the difference between the Muslim "dimije" outfit and the type of clothes that you identified as Serb clothes that Milan Lukic brought for her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: The "dimije" outfit is something typically worn by Muslim women. They are broad-based, and the Serbian skirt is a bit up here, but the difference is huge, so you can tell when you see a Muslim woman wearing Muslim clothes and a Serb woman wearing Serbian clothes. It's easy enough to tell who is who.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You had indicated that he had been unable -- that he'd been able only to obtain permits for his mother and himself and not permits for you and your girlfriend. What was discussed at that point in time? What was the plan as to how the removal from Visegrad was to be accomplished at that point in time, the removal of your girlfriend and yourself from Visegrad at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: The plan was for her to put on this Serb uniform, which she did, and for us to go as far as a bridge, just before the check-point that was there on that road, and they checked people there. They checked people's documents. He had bought her this uniform. My girlfriend put it on, and we were off to Priboj, and then we stopped at this bridge. We all came out there with the exception of his mother. This is a narrow bridge. He took us across the bridge, took us another hundred metres further down and said, Now we're in Serbia; we'll take that unsurfaced road that joins the main road to Priboj one point, and they would be waiting for us there, once he had crossed the check-point with the documents and everything. So that's what we did. We reached the main road to Priboj and Belgrade. We went on for about another kilometre, keeping to the right side of the road because he said it would be easier for him to pick us up that way and he would recognise us immediately. About a kilometre further down the road, we found Milan Lukic there in the vehicle. He was waiting for us already because he had crossed earlier on. He didn't linger at any point along the road. He had the documents and all. So we got back into the car, and we continued our journey to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm looking back in the transcript. I may have missed it, but did you mention the date when you set out in this manner for Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: The 7th.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for us if you had occasion to stop anywhere along the way to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: We stopped once, no more than that, to refuel. We drank coffee. But that was just a single stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you eventually arrive in the city of Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What time of day was it when you arrived in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Dusk, thereabouts. Afternoon, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you arrived in Belgrade, where was it that you arrived and/or stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I think it's called Bezanijska Kosa, so in a flat there, in that area, a white brick building, a bit dull. It was on the second floor or third floor of that building, the flat I mean. It's a flat of some considerable size. I remember there was a bar there, the sort of thing you find in a pub, a counter, and in our room there was a conjugal bed with some black leather on it, that was the dominant material, and a large terrace. I remember that too. I think there's a view opening from that terrace onto a large playground for kids, you know, or -- and a large parking-lot, and this is roughly about what I remember. I can't remember anything more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you advised at any time whose apartment this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: His. He said it was his.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at this apartment on Bezanijska Kosa or at the location Bezanijska Kosa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And during the time that you were staying at that apartment, did you have occasion to leave that apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No. He did; we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And where did Mr. Lukic and his mother reside during the time-period that you were in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: In that same flat in a different room.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what did you and your -- did you have occasion to talk with Mr. Lukic and/or his mother during the time-period that you were -- that you were in the apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, we talked, just like that, about problems, sort of stuff that was going on. That's the sort of thing we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have occasion to make any plans with your girlfriend and/or Mr. Lukic as to what your plans would be in Belgrade or beyond Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: During our time in Belgrade in that flat, we were thinking about where we should go next and how. However, my girlfriend came up with the idea of going to Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the idea of going to Nov i Pazar, did she give any rationales as to why she proposed Novi Pazar as a destination for the two of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. She said she had a friend over there who was doing the same sort of work as she, a waitress, that is, from Novi Pazar. So that's what decided us. We decided to go to Novi Pazar to see her.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for those of us that are not familiar with the geography or makeup of the region, where is the municipality of Novi Pazar located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Novi Pazar is in Serbia, but it's predominantly Muslim. There are few Serbs living there. It's predominantly Muslim. How shall I put this? This was a better place for us to try and organise ourselves in terms of moving on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could focus for a moment on the -- did you at any point in time actually set out for Novi Pazar from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. Once we had devised this plan to go to Novi Pazar, we asked Lukic to drive us there. Would you do that, we said, and he said, Yes, I would. He agreed to take me and my girlfriend there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And if we could focus for a moment on the departure from Belgrade. First of all, what day -- what date did you set out for Novi Pazar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall what time of day or what time of day it was that you set out from Belgrade for Novi Pazar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Sometime about noon I think because we got there at about 8.00 p.m. We drove up to a hotel that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did -- you mentioned to a hotel that was there. What was the ultimate destination in Novi Pazar that you had planned or agreed to go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Our ultimate destination was to get in touch with this friend, my girlfriend's colleague, and see if she could do anything for us in terms of us moving on, going somewhere else from there. We never meant to stay in Novi Pazar. It was just deciding where you were likely to find more Muslims so that you had more people to talk to in terms of arranging yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can go back for a second, you mentioned a hotel. What role did that hotel play in your plans or activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: We spent a night there. The next day my girlfriend, you know, got in touch with this colleague of hers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Before we get to the next day, I want to still finish up on that day when you arrived in Novi Pazar. First of all, who all was present in the automobile for this journey from Belgrade to Novi Pazar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: My girlfriend, I, Milan, and Milan's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say you drove up to the hotel that was there, what happened at that point in time? When you arrived at the hotel, what did Milan and/or his mother do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: When we arrived at the hotel, we said good-bye to them. We thanked them and wished them all the best because of everything they had done for us. Nevertheless, they didn't stay for a very long time. We were there to put ourselves up, and they drove on, but I have no idea where it was that they went to next.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the hotel where you -- where you put yourselves up, that hotel there, is it -- where is it in relation to Novi Pazar? Is it near any type of known landmarks in Novi Pazar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. There's some sort of fortress nearby. The bus terminal isn't too far away, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You indicated that while you were at the hotel, Milan Lukic and his mother left and drove on and you have no idea where they went. Did you have occasion to encounter or see Mr. Milan Lukic in person at any point in time thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, getting back to what you had started telling us about the next day, tell us what happened with respect to your girlfriend and her -- and her colleague or friend.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: The next day, my girlfriend got in touch with this colleague. We spent an hour or two talking, all three of us, exploring avenues for us to leave Novi Pazar and move on somewhere else. She told us that there were certain avenues that were open. I then decided to use these same channels for my father and brother because my parents stayed behind and they had no idea what was going on with me, so I decided to use those channels to evacuate them as well. I took a bus back into town, but they stayed there. My girlfriend and this colleague of hers stayed right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in the -- in the transcript, it is recorded that you "... took the bus back into town, but they stayed there." Could you please repeat your answer and give us the details as to what town you went to and where your girlfriend and this colleague of hers stayed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: My girlfriend stayed with her colleague in Novi Pazar, and I went back to my own town to get my parents. When I say "my own town," I mean Visegrad. That's where I'd left from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, could you detail for us again the manner of the route that you took, if you know, to get to Visegrad from Novi Pazar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: There's a bus that takes you from Novi Pazar to Sarajevo, and it drove across Serbia, Priboj, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, what happened when you returned to Visegrad? Were you able to find your father and brother and retrieve them so as to escape to Novi Pazar as you had intended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: When I came back to Visegrad, the situation was not really, you know, the way it had been when I was leaving. People were no longer staying at their homes but, rather, were hiding in the surrounding woods, keeping together in small groups. So later when we fled the area altogether, they all assembled to form this somewhat larger group. I think that it was July by this time already, so we went on to Medjedja, Gorazde, and all those places there. It's a long road. My brother had been injured at one point.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not understand the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you repeat the last sentence, Witness. Would you please repeat the last sentence. The interpreter didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I returned to Visegrad, when I came back to look for my parents, my father and my brother, I didn't actually find them at home but, rather, in a forest near the houses. It had taken me about two or three days to find them because they didn't dare respond. That was the one thing, and the other thing was no one was willing to give their whereabouts away to me. When I eventually got in touch with them, I came up with several proposals - we can do this, we can do that - and I had realised myself when I was back in Visegrad that the situation was nothing like it had been. It kept deteriorating on a daily basis. We couldn't go the way (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can perhaps have some of these details relating to the brother and the doctor that treated him redacted. Otherwise, it might lead to identification of the witness, and we'd like to preserve his protected identity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I speak, I cannot ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise, Your Honours. Was there more detail that was required? This was a question of the Chamber that prompted this response, so -- before I intervened to obtain the redactions to protect the witness, so I apologise. I don't know. If there's -- more detail is needed, I defer to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: MLD1, did you in fact at any point in time thereafter have an opportunity to reunite with your girlfriend in Novi Pazar as had been your ultimate plan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, was that already elicited that he had an ultimate plan to reunite with her? If not, I'd object to the leading nature of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, he detailed for us the manner in which he intended to return to Novi Pazar with his brother and his father and how that did not come to pass, and he just gives the detail of the direction he went into, so I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise. If I could just get a transcript reference, and I'll correct myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Absolutely, Your Honours. One moment, please. It's at page 21, 2 through 10. He talks about the discussions he and his girlfriend had with a colleague and his decision to try and bring the father and brother there so they could evacuate, as well, in that manner. The description of -- the description of how he discussed with his brother and father the plan to go and how that was nixed was from page 22, lines 13 through my intervention at page 23, line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, but I'm still unable to see where the plan was to reunite with his girlfriend in Novi Pazar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Nor have I seen it, Mr. Ivetic. Is that something we are to deduce? Reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to ever reunite with your girlfriend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't. I made inquiries how I could find her through all the possible connections. Well, to tell you the truth, I did love her a lot, but what's happened has happened. I mean, I gave her a ring; I got engaged to her, and unfortunately, I found out that she is no longer among the living.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I have no further questions in direct examination. I may have questions after my colleague on the other side has concluded. I wish to thank you for coming and answering my questions, and I now pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: MLD1, my name is Dermot Groome. I'm going to be asking you some questions here this morning. I want to make clear to you from the very outset of my questions that I believe most if not all of what you've testified to here today is false. Do you understand? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I do understand, but that's something that you think. I wanted to come and to speak and to talk about what I know before this Tribunal, and as far as I know one should speak the truth when one is here, and I don't know how somebody else would know better than I what I lived through and what I experienced. That's what I think. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, sir, I certainly hope that you honour the oath that you took here today, and it's my intention to question you here today and that in a few weeks introduce proof that will clearly establish that your evidence was not truthful. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I understand, but I don't know how somebody other than me can prove things that I experience. That's the only thing that I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, sir, let's begin. I'd like to show you a photograph. I'm going to ask you to simply look at the photograph. It's a photograph of a location. I'm going to ask you simply to tell us, do you recognise where it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask that Exhibit -- or ERN number 0103-8569 be placed on the screen for the witness to view.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, this is actually another photograph of the same location. But let me ask that OTP number 26, page 5, be shown to you, and it's a closer shot of the neighbourhood that I'd like you to look at. Sir, now, if you could study the roads there, the general layout of the houses, then I'd ask you, can you identify it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, lots of places look alike. I'm not sure. I could see I think the Drina a little bit earlier, but I don't know. Maybe this is somewhere in the direction of Drinsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I will not say the name of this location in open session. I will say that it is a photograph of where you say you were born in your statement. Is it your evidence that you don't recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object as I believe the witness's answer was that he couldn't tell from this perspective. How could he have a perspective of his birth village from the air as Mr. Groome suggests? I mean, there would have to be a foundation laid that at some point in time he had flown over his home village and had an opportunity to previously record such --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness answer the question, please. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure about what place. This place you say is my village, but I really cannot recognise it from this view.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that your statement be called up before you, and I'd ask that it not be broadcast to the public. That is Y0182208.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if we could go to the second page initially, I would like the witness to take a look at his signature and verify that it is in fact his signature. I apologise, Mr. Van Hooydonk advised me that I should be saying Y0182206, the English translation of the statement. Hopefully that will bring up both copies. And if we could go to the second page for the signature line.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, there's a signature now that's partly covered by a seal. Do you recognise that signature as your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this the statement that you gave in relation to this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, just above your signature, correct me if I'm wrong, the statement says or what is on the document here before us says: "This statement was given voluntarily and not under threat, force, false belief, or fraud. By my signature, I confirm the authenticity of it." And then your signature appears. Did you give such a statement under those conditions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And next to your signature, it's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: This is my signature. As it says, voluntarily, without threats, to this lady, this lady, I don't know. She was the first one to contact me about this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, next to your signature it states: "Statement taken by Jelena Rasic, case manager." Is that the name of the lady that took your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It looks as though the statement was then sworn before a judge or some other public official in Sarajevo on the 26th of March, 2008. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the official was? Was it a judge? Was it some other public official? Who was the person who you appeared before and signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: It was in the court building on the ground floor where documents are certified or notarised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you signed this statement, were you standing before that official?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before signing it, did you read it carefully?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to read without any difficulty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps if I had glasses it would be easier, but yes, I can read. I mean, the letters are small, but I can see it, if you are thinking of what I'm seeing in front of me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was actually referring to the time that you swore out -- or you signed the statement, but let me ask you now that you raise it, do you have glasses with you that would assist you? I will be asking you to look at the screen several times during the course of your testimony. You are free to take out glasses if you have them with you. If not, perhaps we might be able to find a pair of reading glasses that you might be able to use. Do you have glasses with you here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: If necessary. I mean, if I get stuck somewhere I can ask for some, but if I need to read something, it's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Please let us know if you do. Now, going back to the day you signed this statement, did you read it carefully before you signed it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes. First we talked; then I read the statement; then we went to the court building, to the ground floor where documents like this are notarised; then we notarised it, like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The first time that -- was this the same day as the first time that you met Jelena Rasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that you spoke with her. Where were you when you spoke with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: In Sarajevo. First, she called me on the phone to meet in Sarajevo. She explained the situation why she came. She said she was from the team, on the cases, and then that Milan knows that you -- that I did this and this and that he was asking me if I would be willing to testify, and I signed the statement. We went to the court building, and then if necessary, I also said that I would come here, and then after, we talked about the situation and being a protected witness and so on. I mean, I really couldn't wait to have the opportunity to talk about my experiences --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: -- about these dates, because, yeah, as a matter of fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: -- I saw all sorts of things on television and on newspaper. I don't know if that's true or not. I'm only here to speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm reluctant to interrupt you because once I turn on my microphone, your voice then gets carried out to the public. But it's very important that you answer my questions directly. You've been able now to testify about the dates and everything you came to testify. I have very specific questions. I'd appreciate if you could just answer them as briefly as possible, okay? My question was, where did you meet Jelena Rasic? You've said Sarajevo. Can I ask you specifically, where did you meet? Was it in an office, in your home, in a commercial establishment? Where was it that you met?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: We were in a restaurant, in some house. We were in these two places.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Which place were you in first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: First we were in a house or in the restaurant. I really don't remember. I don't know if this is important where we were first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It actually is, sir. You don't remember which one you were in first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, the cafe, the restaurant is nearby. We were in the house first to talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, whose house was it, and if saying that compromises your identity, I'll ask Judge Robinson to go into closed session. Can you answer whose house you were in without compromising your identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not aware of whose house it was. I didn't ask anything like that. All I asked was, Is it safe here? Is it safe. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I do, sir. How did you get to the house that morning or that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: She got in touch with me. She told me to come to the cafe where we met. Then we met there, and then we went to talk, to a safe place that nobody would - as they say - discovery my identity, and then when she explained to me why she had come to me and would I be willing to provide a written statement, this, what's written here, and I said that I would. And when the statement was written, it was given to me to read, and when I read the statement, we went to this court, to the court building --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: -- on the ground floor, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Again, you should be guided by my questions rather than engage in a long narrative. My question for you is, how long did you remain in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: An hour or two. I don't know. Not long. For as long as we talked, you know, the time that it took for her to say who she was, what her business was, and that she was from these teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What neighbourhood in Sarajevo was this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: In the direction of Bistrik, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was she taking notes as you spoke about the information you provided?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Just something, not really that thoroughly because everything had to be put on paper. She said, Would I be willing to do this, would I be able to provide a statement, and if necessary would I be able to -- or would I agree to come to testify if it was necessary, and I said that I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When were you first presented with the statement that we see here before us today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, the date is right there, when I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did she print this statement for you, or was it already printed when you spoke with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I don't know how she printed it. First, she talked to me, and I told her what is written here first, and then when she wrote the statement, she gave it to me to read, and then when I read it, then I signed it. I don't know how she printed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever see her leave where you were when she -- you were discussing your statement with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a printer in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: There were some things, but I don't know what -- what exactly was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that the first written account that she provided you, the statement, it was accurate the first time, that you didn't ask to make any corrections to it, that everything that was in it was truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: What I told her and what was put on the paper, there were no corrections. Exactly the way I told it to her was the way it was put on the paper, and there were no corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the official that you signed the document before, did that official ask you whether you had read the document and whether you were affirming its accuracy and its truthfulness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: The official -- no, I don't think so. He just took my ID card and he wrote something there. He looked at me. I mean, that's how they usually do it. He said, Is this all right, yes, sign. That was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Jelena Rasic sign her signature before that official as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: We all signed it at this desk counter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your Honour, at this time I would tender into evidence the prior statement of the witness under seal. I also have a copy of the statement which has been redacted. His name and his identifying information has been redacted. I would be tendering that as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one comment as to that. As I see now the version in e-court that's on the screen, the English translation does not in fact match 100 per cent the B/C/S original. It appears that the draft translation that had been prepared earlier in the case is in e-court. The official CLSS translation I have in my --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see that we're very close to the break. I think this will take us to the break. It will influence the testimony of the witness. So could I ask in this one instance that the witness be excused so we can discuss what I believe is a rather important matter with respect to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I had actually planed to just break the sessions into two halves and go a little beyond an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, I'll be guided by the Chamber then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We can hear Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The official seal says translation of the B/C/S, and, of course, the B/C/S original which is on the left-hand side of the screen does not contain the village that is listed as the birth place on the first page in the English translation that's in e-court, so that was all I was going to point out and, if need be, arrange for the official translation to be put into e-court if this document is going to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact, let me just correct a couple of things, Your Honour. That's not a CLSS translation. That's the translation that the Defence provided. They provided a translation which indicates the place of birth of this witness. Then they provided a photocopy of the original statement where the place of birth is actually removed from the document. If you look at the first page of the original, although it says "place of birth," "place of birth" has been removed from the photocopy. So it is my intention at this stage to ask the Defence to please produce the original of the document so that I may view it over the course of the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was the other reason I rose. I have it here, the original of the documents, the two -- it looks like there's two originals of the documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could see both.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- and the translation from CLSS. The one that's on the screen is the Defence draft translation. The official CLSS is being -- is in this packet. If I could have the usher 's assistance to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, show it to counsel and then to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I then ask Mr. Ivetic to give some explanation as to why the original translation that was provided to the Prosecution listed the name of the birth place of this witness as the place that it does? What's the explanation for that, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. The Chamber is viewing the document. Mr. Groome, tell us your point again. You are saying the translation ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the original submission of the Defence with respect to the alibi witness, we were provided with the alibi notice of this witness plus two statements: the purported original -- a photocopy of the original plus a copy of a translation done by the Defence themselves. If you look at a copy of the translation that we were provided by the Defence, the town or the place of birth of this witness is listed, and I don't know whether he was actually born there or not, so I won't say it, but it's a location very relevant to this case. Yet when we look at the photocopy of the original we were provided, the place of birth is simply removed from the document. There is no place of birth in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do we have what was provided to you by the Defence with the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's on the screen, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's on --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What I've been provided is on the screen. It's the very first line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see that now. Yes. Mr. Ivetic, what's the explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can surmise based upon what I know and give you the information. Perhaps I can defer if I misstate anything to Mr. Alarid, since this predates me. But it's my understanding that at the time that the alibi statements of this witness and several other witnesses were prepared and tendered, there is a short dead-line and a requirement to hand those over. So rather than -- at that point in time CLSS official translations were not available, and our staff, including, I believe, Ms. Jelena Rasic, created draft translations of this statement and several other statements. If one compares the translation that is on the screen as the English translation and the one that CLSS prepared, you'll see the quality of the translation differs significantly, and I can only surmise that in translating several statements at the same time under those circumstances that an error occurred in the English translation of this document. The witness did testify in private session at page 7, lines 24 and onward, I believe, as to the actual village from whence he hails, so the witness has given sworn testimony as to, I believe, where he hails from. But the Prosecutor is free to question on that. I just -- it's my understanding that official translations are the ones that are supposed to be tendered into evidence, and I happen to have caught that while looking at the screen and seeing the -- the translation that's in the system as not being the one that I was looking off of in front of me. And that's why I rose to bring it to the Court's attention, and that's -- I don't know the date of that original submission, but it would have been sometime shortly after trial commenced, I believe. Perhaps -- it was before trial commenced, slightly before the trial commenced when there was the dead-line to produce this witness's and, I believe, I think a dozen other witnesses' statements, and I believe in those statements that were at that point in time translated hurriedly and produced. There are several other witnesses who do hail from the village that is mentioned in this translation that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you saying that the place of birth that is on the statement which is on the screen is wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The place of birth is not on the original B/C/S statement, Your Honour. The original B/C/S that Your Honours have and the one that's in the system does not have a place of birth listed for this witness. It merely says date and place of birth, and it has the date. It does not have the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I'm asking whether the place of birth given in this statement that is on the screen, whether you are contesting that that is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The translation has an erroneous place of birth, I believe, yes, based upon the witness's testimony at page 7, line 24, and 8, line 1, wherein he mentioned the village he is from. I cannot be 100 per cent sure because my question didn't deal where you were born. I asked, Where did you live in 1992? We can ask the witness to clarify that for us. He is the one who would know. I honestly, as I stand here, do not know the precise place of birth of this witness. I only know what I have on the record and what I can see with my own eyes and my knowledge of B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, maybe I can ask a few more questions of the witness, but we're not talking about a mistranslation here. We're talking about information that seems to have been omitted in what purports is now what is an original and seems to have mysteriously inserted itself into a translation. If I could ask the witness a few more questions to see what he may know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to address briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid, emphasis on briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And briefly I just say, I mean, I surmise that it was a typographical sort of word-processing mistake that Ms. Rasic did. The quality of her translation I've always had a problem. She usually uses a disk to break things up and attempt translations, so I would defer to the CLSS translation, and I can't understand why we would -- obviously the Bosnian draft was created first, so it was an oversight or a mistake on the English translation by Ms. Rasic. I would not consider her translation official.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Right. So you say it was done inadvertently. Mr. Groome, yes. Do you want to ask a few more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you've been listening to our conversation here. When you read your statement and at the very first line it said your place of birth, what followed that? Did it have your place of birth after your -- in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you to rely on your recollection rather than reading the document in front of you. When you read the document, thinking back to March when you read the document, the first line where it indicated your place of birth, do you have a recollection as to whether or not it had your place of birth indicated in the original statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I don't remember that sort of detail. I looked at my name, my family name, date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this came up in the middle of me tendering the two exhibits --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place of birth, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It came up when I was in the middle of tendering a sealed unredacted version and a public redacted version. I would re-tender those at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, Your Honour, I have no objection to the original B/C/S of the statement coming in and the CLSS translation of that original coming in. I can -- I don't have Ms. O'Leary here today to be able to find out how long it would take to get that CLSS translation into e-court, but I can -- I'm sure we can be in touch with the Registrar to ensure that that is done so that we have the official translation. I -- by all means, if Mr. Groome needs a copy, he can have the copy that I believe is still in Your Honours' possession of the translation, if that's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I prepared my examination based on the translation that the Defence provided me, so I will continue with that. They are certainly free to introduce other translations on their redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the unredacted version will become Exhibit P226 under seal, and redacted version of the statement will become Exhibit P227.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to take the break now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, after the day that you signed the statement, how many times did you meet with Jelena Rasic after that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Once or so. I don't know. Not too many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it possible that it's more than once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that. I met the lawyer later on, this lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "this lawyer," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: That one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it Mr. Ivetic who questioned you here this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yeah, that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the purpose of meeting Jelena Rasic after you had signed your sworn statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Just to make sure whether I go or not, was I facing any problems, you know, that sort of stuff, did anyone blow my cover or not, does anyone know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many times did you meet with Mr. Ivetic prior to testifying today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were both of those times in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No. Once in Sarajevo and once in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, it's all about this, the same thing, similar, where there any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that the very first time that you met with Jelena Rasic, you were presented with a typed copy of this statement complete with everything except your name and that the only thing that was missing from the statement was information about you, your name and your date of birth. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I also put it to you that the only real conversation that took place between you and Jelena Rasic that day, was whether you would agree to give or testify to the facts described in this statement and how much money you would require to do that. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the English has already been asked. He's putting his case. I'll allow it. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, you said in your testimony that Jelena Rasic told you that you would be a protected witness. Was this the first time that you met Jelena Rasic that she told you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: When we talked, I asked to be protected. If not, I can't go. I couldn't agree to go for the reason that I've specified already, and this thing that I signed, all this info was there. It's not like something was missing. Name, surname, all that it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But you recognise now that the place where you were born is missing from the document that you see before you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Missing, yes, but I don't think it was there either. I don't know how they go about their business. I read that this was me, this was my statement and that I signed it and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, when you told Jelena Rasic on the 26th of March, 2008, that you would only testify as a protected witness, what did she tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: That she would see whether this was a possibility, will someone allow, what do I know. The court probably if they allow, I really don't know how exactly this works.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When were you told that you were going to be given protections, that your identity would not be revealed to anyone outside this courtroom when you testified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Before I signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you were told prior to signing the statement on the 26th of March, 2008, that you would be given protections by this court and your identity would not be revealed to anyone outside of this courtroom. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was promised. And the last time we met, I was adamant, Is that it? Yes. Just in case I'm here and is it true or not or what.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you have signed the statement or would you have agreed to testify without being given that promise by Jelena Rasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: That's a bit more difficult for me to sign -- you know what? I said it. Come to sign this and something public like this, me not being protected and all, I said, No good for me, you see? That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you realise it was not until six months after that day that the Chamber finally did extend you protective measures on the 24th of September, 2008?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object as to foundation. How can the witness know what's been transpiring in these proceedings, and I object to the relevance of these questions as to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing that question, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you obtain a passport for your trip up here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yeah. Can't do without one, can I?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that the first time you had a -- was that the first passport that you've owned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No. In Visegrad in Republika Srpska, yes, when I signed up for my return that I used to have a passport over there, the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When were you issued your first passport? What year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: I don't know. After the war. After the war, thereabouts. There was this neighbour of mine. I went to work for him and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I don't need the entire account of how you received the passport. If you tell me that it was after the war, that's sufficient for my purposes. My next question is, your girlfriend, did she have a passport that you knew of during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go into closed session for a few minutes and ask you some questions about your family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we might do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, is it your testimony that lived with your girlfriend in her apartment in Dusce or simply that you lived at home and visited her at the apartment from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: You could say that I practically lived there. I spent the night there often. I stopped by often. I was with her most of the time, and I didn't see anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you say that you were dating her for five to six months, so that would mean in -- your relationship with her began in January or February of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us when it was that you began regularly staying at her apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a regular thing. What I understood you to be asking is if I was there day and night. Is that what you mean by regularly?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, the transcript on page 48, line 4, records you as saying "I practically lived there." So my question to you is, can you approximate for us when it was that you practically lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Yes, yes, practically. I agree with that, practically. The first half of our relationship, we saw each other less frequently. Than we would meet more and more often. We got close. We fell in love. We loved each other. Well, I hope that's nothing of dispute. Everyone has a right to fall in love.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: And even if they did not, I did fall in love with her, and I was in love with her at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No, I was living at home, but for the last two or three months I would be going there often, and sometimes I would spend the night there, maybe one night or sometimes two nights, but I lived with my family normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm quite concerned that Mr. Groome in -- in cross-examination of every single one of our protected witnesses mentions identifying details in open session. He has now identified the village this gentleman is from. He did that with MLD10, as well, and that was played on SENSE Agency, et cetera. So we are quite concerned with this tactic of Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think it's a tactic. I'm sure it's done inadvertently. That will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I want to look at another point in your statement. The first mention in your statement about you having any interaction with the police in Visegrad gives that date, the 4th of June. You do not mention anything prior to that happening to you or your family. Did anything happen to you or your family prior to the 4th of June with respect to the police or soldiers in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: With the army, the soldiers, yes, and with the police at the time -- well, actually the soldiers took me to the stadium. I was detained and so on. There were such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you were detained by the soldiers -- when were you detained by the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: We went to the stadium in mid-April. After that, they would be going through the villages, walking through them, and then at one time they took us allegedly to the police. Actually, they took us to the police station. Finally, they took us to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was that with a person by the name of Fadil Jelacic? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Fadil Jelacic, yes. That's the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let me just summarise the event and ask you whether or not I'm accurately portraying it. That one day in your village, Fadil was hiding in the woods with Ibrahim Demir and Himo Sepo when about 30 soldiers entered the village. The soldiers entered the village and captured three people, two men, one who was Semso Becirovic and a young boy by the name of Almir Mesic. The soldiers took the three prisoners and told Fadil's father if Fadil did not turn himself by the time of night fell, the three hostages would be killed. The three men, frightened, were taken away and later that evening Fadil, afraid for the lives of his friends, turned himself in. Because he turned himself in, those three people were not killed. You are one of the men that was taken in that Fadil tried to save by turning himself in. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: No. No, it's not true. There is something about that, but I can tell my version of it. I mean, it wasn't like that. It happened differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you detained by the police the same day that Fadil came later and turned himself in?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The transcript -- the audio did carry the name of the brother, I believe, and one other individual. I'd ask that those be redacted to protect the identity of this protected witness. Thank you. That's in line numbers 2 and 3 of page 51, I believe, where this came up, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That will be done. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, MLD1, if I could move ahead to what happened at the police station. You were detained at the police station in Visegrad for quite a number of days; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Three or four days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And one of the people that you were detained there with was a man by the name of Nezir Zunic; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Zunic, yes. Zunic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you were present when he was taken out by Niko Vujicic, and he has never been seen since; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: He stayed after I left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess I'm wondering where this is going to and what this relevance is as to this particular case and the particular testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome will explain. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: One of the people he encountered during that visit was Milan Lukic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall a person by the name of Safet Tvrtkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: Tvrtkovic, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He was with you in the Visegrad police station, and he was taken out by Novo Rajak. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD1
utterances.text: They all stayed after I left. While I was there those two or three days, only those from the Uzice Corps came to beat us and to abuse us, but they stayed after I left. I was only there for two or three days. I, Sasa, Stjepan, and Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I have information from one of these men that Milan Lukic visited that police station nearly every night while you were there. Do you deny that this is not true?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a minute. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe that we're again having Mr. Groome trying to introduce statements of out-of-court declarants that are unavailable for cross-examination, trying to introduce them into these proceedings through a witness that -- at least with this type of question, there's no ability for there to be a foundation to know whether this witness has any kind of means of knowing about or testifying about what someone else allegedly told Mr. Groome. I would hold Mr. Groome to the same standards that were held against the Defence in the cross-examination of Prosecution witnesses, namely that the statements of out-of-court declarants cannot be presented to witnesses to assert the truth of the matter that is asserted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope this is not coming out of my time. I'm simply asking the witness, did he see Milan Lukic there during the two or three days that he was held captive there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think you have misread it. I mean, he's simply putting to him that Milan Lukic visited him at the police station every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
